html:
The Pequot War was a war in southern New England from 1636 to 1638 between the Pequot people of eastern Connecticut and the English colonies, with their Native allies the Mohegan and the Narragansett. It ended with the near destruction of the Pequot as a nation.

The Pequot were the strongest power on the Connecticut coast and controlled the trade in wampum shell beads with the Dutch. English settlers from Massachusetts Bay were moving into the Connecticut valley, among peoples such as the Tunxis and the Podunk. The killing of English traders in 1634 and 1636 led to a Massachusetts raid, and the Pequot hit back at the new towns.

In May 1637 English troops under John Mason and John Underhill, with Mohegan warriors led by Uncas and Narragansett allies, surrounded the Pequot fort at Mystic and set it on fire. Several hundred people, most of them women, children and old men, died. The survivors were hunted down. Their leader Sassacus fled west and was killed by the Mohawk.

The Treaty of Hartford in 1638 declared the Pequot nation dissolved. Captives were handed to the Mohegan and Narragansett, and some were shipped as slaves to the West Indies. English settlement then spread along the coast, into the lands of peoples such as the Hammonasset. The war set the pattern for King Philip's War forty years later.
